implementation_notes: The BCL supplies both halves: Lazy<T> in its default LazyThreadSafetyMode.ExecutionAndPublication runs the wrapped factory exactly once, and ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd provides the atomic keyed registration. Store a Lazy<Task<TValue>> rather than a Task: GetOrAdd's value factory may run on several threads under contention, but each contender builds only a Lazy whose Value the losers never touch, so duplicating the Lazy object is harmless while duplicating the async call is not. Any number of callers may await the same Task; remove the entry when it completes - for example from a continuation that calls TryRemove - so the dictionary stays an in-flight registry instead of silently becoming a result cache.
pitfalls: Never store a bare Task built by a naive GetOrAdd lambda: the value factory may run concurrently on several threads, so the underlying call would start more than once; wrap it in Lazy<T> (ExecutionAndPublication) so only the stored instance's Value is produced.
Await the shared task; .Result/.Wait() blocks a thread for the whole flight and can deadlock under a SynchronizationContext.
A CancellationToken belongs to the caller, not the flight: one caller's token must not cancel the shared task - give the flight its own token or a linked one.
Every waiter observes the same faulted Task, so exception stacks point at the leader; log the flight, not only each awaiting handler.
Remove the entry when the task completes: a dictionary that keeps completed tasks is a growing cache with none of a cache's eviction or invalidation.
